title: Bahrani Dynasty
capsule: From the mid-thirteenth century the historical region of Bahrayn in eastern Arabia—the oasis of al-Ahsa, the port of Qatif, and the islands of Bahrain—was governed by a succession of Arab dynasties drawn largely from the Banu Uqayl of the Banu Amir confederation. The Usfurids, founded by Usfur ibn Rashid around 1253, ruled from al-Ahsa and overthrew the older Uyunids, though after 1320 the princes of Hormuz contested control of Bahrain and Qatif. The Shi'i Twelver Jarwanids, based at Qatif, displaced the Usfurids in the late fourteenth century and held the region until about 1417, when they were in turn supplanted by the Jabrids (Banu Jabr); under Ajwad ibn Zamil (d. 1496) the Jabrids commanded much of the peninsula until Migrin ibn Zamil was killed resisting a Portuguese attack near Bahrain in 1521 and the Ottomans absorbed al-Ahsa into the Lahsa Eyalet.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political history of the dynasty is reasonably attested in Arabic chronicles, but its territorial limits across eastern Arabia are poorly mapped and boundaries are approximate; the batch QID and Wikipedia link to Al-Ahsa Oasis suggest the dataset conflates multiple overlapping dynasties in the region.
